report.summary: Reviewed chunk 7 of 8 of publish.py: contains publish_to_pr, read_pr_thread, _parse_comment definitions with docstrings and comments.
risks: publish_to_pr | high | Uses screen_egress before runner invocation; if screen_egress raises instead of returning a tuple, the function may crash. | Check screen_egress implementation to confirm it always returns a tuple or None.
publish_to_pr | medium | The gate runs before dry_run check; dry_run may be blocked by secret floor, which might be unintended. | Confirm design intent: should dry_run bypass the gate?

read_pr_thread | medium | Uses screen_egress with only pr and repo; but comment body is not screened, potentially leaking sensitive content. | Verify if comment body screening is handled elsewhere or if this is a gap.

handoff.purpose: Contains publish_to_pr and read_pr_thread public functions, and _parse_comment helper.

claims.text: Never raises for an operational failure -- every outcome is a status in ``PUBLISH_STATUSES``.
claims.why: PUBLISH_STATUSES is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify that all paths return a status in that set.

claims.text: ``dry_run=True`` renders and gates but does NOT invoke the runner at all; the markdown comes back on the result.
claims.why: Code checks screen_egress first, then returns early with dry_run status and markdown, never calling runner.

claims.text: The gate still runs, so a dry run is an honest rehearsal rather than a way around the floor.
claims.why: screen_egress is called before the dry_run check; if it hits, dry_run is not returned.

claims.text: The body goes to gh on STDIN via ``--body-file -``: a deliberation exceeds the Windows argv limit, and stdin keeps the payload inspectable by a fake runner in tests exactly as argv would be.
claims.why: Code constructs argv with '--body-file', '-' and passes body as stdin to runner; no truncation or alternative method is used.

claims.text: Never raises for an operational failure; every outcome is a status in ``READ_STATUSES``.
claims.why: READ_STATUSES is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify that all paths return a status in that set.

claims.text: Nothing read here is authoritative: a reply is INPUT to a later round, not a verdict, and it is not on the hash-chained bus until the council appends it there.
claims.why: Function returns ThreadResult with turns parsed from comments; no bus or hash-chain operation is performed.

claims.text: Tolerant of the two author shapes gh uses (``author.login`` from the GraphQL-backed ``pr view --json``, ``user.login`` from the REST-backed ``gh api``).
claims.why: The function body is truncated; only the first few lines are visible, showing extraction of author_obj but not the full handling. Cannot confirm tolerance for both shapes.

observations.what: publish_to_pr calls screen_egress before checking dry_run; if secret floor fires, dry_run is not honored.
read_pr_thread calls screen_egress with only pr and repo, not the comment body; body is not screened.
_parse_comment docstring claims tolerance for two author shapes, but the code shown only extracts author_obj; the rest is cut off.
